Rashi on Eruvin 27b:11:1.hebrew: דאם כן - דצאן לאו למישרי גיזות הוא דאתא, אלא עור — לא הוה כתיב קרא צאן, אלא בקר, דלית ליה גיזות:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:11:1.english: For if so - That [if] "sheep" did not come to permit fleece, but rather [the] hide — the verse would not have written "sheep," but rather "oxen," which has no fleece.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:13:1.hebrew: במאי קא מיפלגי רבי יהודה ורבי אליעזר - דאמרי תרוייהו דגים ניקחין, ובציר הוא דפליגי:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:13:1.english: With regard to what do Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Eliezer disagree - For both of them say [that] fish may be purchased, and it is [only] regarding brine that they disagree.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:13:2.hebrew: והני תנאי דלקמן - דדרשי פרי מפרי וגידולי קרקע, וולד ולדות הארץ, ותרוייהו ממעטי דגים, וכ"ש ציר:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:13:2.english: And these tanna’im below - Who expound [the verse to include only] “produce of produce and grown from the ground” and “offspring of the offspring of the earth,” and both [opinions] exclude fish, and all the more so [fish] brine.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:14:1.hebrew: ה"ג: לר"א מיעט ציר, ולרבי יהודה מיעט מים ומלח - דלאו ציר:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:14:1.english: This is the correct reading: “According to Rabbi Eliezer it excluded brine, and according to Rabbi Yehuda it excluded water and salt” - For [according to Rabbi Yehuda, it is] not brine [that was excluded].

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:15:1.english: This is the correct reading: “As it was taught: ‘And you shall bestow the money...’”:

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:15:2.hebrew: פרי מפרי - עגל נולד מאמו, וכן שה; וענבים מחרצנים, שזורעין החרצנים:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:15:2.english: Produce of produce - A calf is born from its mother, and similarly a lamb; and grapes [come] from grape seeds, as one sows the grape seeds.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:15:3.english: And grown from the ground - For all of them are nourished and grow from the ground.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:16:1.english: Offspring of the offspring of the earth - That were created from the earth during the Act of Creation.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:17:1.hebrew: דגים - גידולי קרקע נינהו — קסבר שהדגים ניזונין מן הקרקע:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:17:1.english: Fish - [As for the statement that] they are grown from the ground — he maintains that fish are nourished from the ground.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:1:1.hebrew: לא נצרכה - הא דמתני ר' יצחק מים ומלח המעורבין ניקחין — אלא כשנתן לתוכן שמן:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:1:1.english: It was only necessary - That which Rabbi Yitzḥak taught, that water and salt mixed together may be purchased [with second-tithe money] — [was stated] only when one put oil into them.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:2:1.hebrew: בהבלעה - בשביל המים והמלח קנה השמן ביוקר, והבליע בו דמיהן; וכי האי גוונא שרי רבי יצחק:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:2:1.english: By inclusion - On account of the water and the salt, he bought the oil at a high price and absorbed their cost into it; and in a case such as this, Rabbi Yitzchak permits [it].

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:1.english: And it was taught - In a calm tone [i.e., as an assertion, not a question].

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:2.hebrew: בבקר - הואיל וכתיב ״בכל אשר תאוה נפשך״, למה לי למיכתב ״בבקר ובצאן וביין ובשכר״? אלא לדרשות: ״בבקר״ — ללמדך שלוקחים בקר אגב עורו, ויצא העור לחולין, ואין צריך למוכרו ולחזור ולאכלו בירושלים:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:2.english: On oxen - Since it is written: “On all that your heart desires,” why do I need [the verse] to write “On oxen, and on sheep, and on wine, and on strong drink”? Rather, [they are written] for expositions: “On oxen” — to teach you that one may purchase an ox along with its hide, and the hide becomes non-sacred, and one does not need to sell it and subsequently consume [its proceeds] in Jerusalem.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:3.hebrew: אגב גיזותיה - אע"ג דאיכא תרתי — עור וגיזה — דנפקי לחולין:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:3.english: Along with its fleece - Even though there are two [items] — hide and fleece — that become non-sacred.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:4.hebrew: אגב קנקן - חבית של חרס שהיין שמור בתוכו, ויצא הקנקן לחולין:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:4.english: Along with [its] jug - An earthenware jar in which the wine is kept, and the jug assumes non-sacred status.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:5.hebrew: תמד - שנותנים מים בחרצנים, ולכשהחמיץ — שנגמרה תסיסתו — הוי כיין. אלמא, מדקתני "בבקר" אגב עורו, אלמא בהבלעה שרי, ואע"ג דעור באנפי נפשיה לא חזי, דמידי דמאכל בעינן, כדכתיב "ואכלת":
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:3:5.english: Temed - Where they put water into grape seeds; and once it has fermented — meaning that its fermentation is complete — it is like wine. Thus, from [the fact] that it teaches: “On oxen,” [that it may be bought] along with its hide, it is evident that [purchase] by inclusion is permitted, even though hide on its own is not suitable [for purchase with tithe funds], for we require an item of food, as it is written: “And you shall eat.”

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:4:1.english: Whoever interprets “oxen” - That it was necessary to write it according to ben Bag Bag, etc.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:5:1.hebrew: עורו - המחובר לבשר, ואינו יכול להפשיטו מחיים:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:5:1.english: Its hide - Which is attached to the flesh, and one cannot flay it while [the animal is] alive.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:5:2.hebrew: אבל גיזה - יכול לגוזזה מחיים, והוה אמינא דליתסר, דלא גופא דפירא הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:5:2.english: But fleece - One can shear it while [the animal is] alive, and I would have said that it should be forbidden, as it is not the body of the food [itself].

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:7:1.hebrew: קיוהא - כמו "תקהינה שיניו" (ירמיהו ל״א:ל׳). כלומר: לאו פירא ממש הוא, אלא מים בעלמא שנכנס בהן קיוהא של חרצנים — איגרו"ס בלע"ז:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:7:1.english: Acidity - Like [in the verse]: “His teeth shall be set on edge” (Jeremiah 31:30). That is to say: it is not actual fruit [juice], but mere water into which the acidity of grape seeds has entered — aigros in Old French.

Rashi on Eruvin 27b:8:1.hebrew: ואי כתב שכר הוה אמינא - הבלעה לעולם אסירא, והאי שכר לאו תמד הוא דנילף מיניה דיהיב דמים של מים בהבלעה; אלא האי שכר — דבילה קעילית היא מאותו מקום דמשכרא, כדאמרינן בכריתות (דף יג:): ״אכל דבילה קעילית ונכנס למקדש — חייב״:
Rashi on Eruvin 27b:8:1.english: And if [the Torah] had written “strong drink,” I would have said - Absorption is always forbidden, and this “strong drink” is not *temed*, from which we would derive that one pays the money for the water through absorption; rather, this “strong drink” is dried figs from Ke’ila, from that place, which intoxicate, as we say in Keritot (13b): “One who ate dried figs from Ke’ila and entered the Sanctuary is liable.”

Tosafot on Eruvin 27b:10:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא צאן על גב עורו אין - ואם תאמר: והא נפקא לן מיין אגב קנקן, דעור נמי חשיב שומר, כדאמרי' בהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קיח.)? וי"ל: דעור לא הוי כל כך שומר לבשר, דמשהופשט לא הוי שומר; אבל יין אי אפשר בלא קנקן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 27b:10:1.english: I might have said: A sheep together with its hide, yes - And if you say: But do we not derive [this] from wine together with its jug, for a hide is also considered a protective cover, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaOr VeHaRotev (Chullin 118a)? And one can say: A hide is not such a protective cover for meat, for once it is flayed it is no longer a protective cover; but wine is impossible without a jug.

Tosafot on Eruvin 27b:8:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא מאי שכר דבילה קעילית - כל הני דרשות מיתורא דביתי"ן דריש, דפרטי צריכי לפרט וכלל; דממה נפשך צריכי תרי מינייהו, כדאמר בפרק קמא דקדושין (דף יז.) גבי הענקה: דאי כתיב צאן הוה אמינא גידולי קרקע לא, ואי כתיב גורן הוה אמינא בעלי חיים לא; ושאר פרטי נמי שמא צריכי לשום דרשה. ועוד, דבשבועות פ"ג (דף כג.) ובפרק בתרא דיומא (דף עו.) פריך: ואימא דבילה קעילית? ומשני: גמר "שכר" "שכר" מנזיר. והכא נפקא לן מדמרבינן יין אגב קנקן! אלא התם אצטריך "שכר" "שכר" דלא נימא שכר גופיה דבילה קעילית היא, והכא אבי"ת דבשכר קאי. וקשה: דהיכי קאמר הכא דה"א דבי"ת דבשכר לדבילה קעילית אתא? הא מכלל ופרט נפקא, דהוו פירי מפירי! ועוד הקשה מה"ר שמואל: דהיכי בעי למימר התם דשכר גופיה לדבילה קעילית? והאמר הכא דאי לאו יתור דיין אגב קנקן, ה"א דבי"ת דבשכר לדבילה קעילית! ויש לומר: דשכר גופיה בעי למימר לדבילה קעילית בעינן, והכא בדבילה מעורבת עם המים, שכך רגילים לתקנם, וחשיב טפי מתמד. ואם תאמר: אמאי לא מוכח התם דשתיה בכלל אכילה מדמרבינן תמד, ואמר רחמנא "ואכלת"? וליכא למימר ע"י אניגרון כדאמרינן התם, דמידי דמשכר בעינן, הואיל ואתי מריבויא דבשכר! וי"ל: ד"ואכלת" לא קאי אביתי"ן, אלא אגופיה דקרא, דהא עור וגיזה וקנקן לאו בני אכילה נינהו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 27b:8:1.english: I might have said: What is strong drink? Dried figs from Ke’ila - All these derivations [the Gemara] derives from the superfluity of the [prefixes of the letter] bet, for the specifications [themselves] are needed for [the hermeneutical rule of] a generalization and a specification; for in any case two of them are necessary, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Kiddushin (17a) regarding the severance gift [given to a Hebrew slave]: that if [the verse] had written "flock," I would have said produce of the ground [is] not [included], and if it had written "threshing floor," I would have said living creatures [are] not [included]; and the other specifications as well are perhaps needed for some derivation. Furthermore, in Shevuot chapter 3 (23a) and in the final chapter of Yoma (76a), [the Gemara] asks: "And say [that 'strong drink' means] dried figs from Ke'ila?" And it answers: It derives [by verbal analogy of] "strong drink" [and] "strong drink" from a nazirite. Whereas here, we derive [that it is not dried figs from Ke'ila] from the fact that we include wine along with its jug! Rather, there [in Shevuot and Yoma], "strong drink" [from] "strong drink" was necessary so that we should not say that "strong drink" itself is dried figs from Ke'ila; whereas here [the Gemara] refers to the [prefix of the letter] bet of bashekhar. And this is difficult: For how can [the Gemara] say here that I might have said that the bet of bashekhar comes [to include] dried figs from Ke'ila? Surely that is derived from [the rule of] a generalization and a specification, as they are produce of produce [i.e., offspring of the earth]! And furthermore, Our Teacher Rabbi Shmuel raised a difficulty: For how could [the Gemara] consider saying there that "strong drink" itself [comes] for dried figs from Ke'ila? Surely [the Gemara] says here that were it not for the superfluity of [including] wine along with its jug, I might have said that the bet of bashekhar [comes] for dried figs from Ke'ila [which presupposes that "strong drink" itself already means a beverage]! And one can answer: That [there, it meant that] we require "strong drink" itself [to mean] dried figs from Ke'ila [in their pure state], whereas here [the Gemara refers to] dried figs mixed with water, for so people were accustomed to prepare them, and it is considered superior to temed. And if you should say: Why does [the Gemara] not prove there [in Shevuot] that drinking is included in [the legal category of] eating from the fact that we include temed, and the Merciful One states, "And you shall eat"? And one cannot say [that it is consumed] by means of anigron [beet juice eaten with bread], as we say there, because we require something that intoxicates, since it comes from the amplification of bashekhar! And one can answer: That "and you shall eat" does not refer to [the extensions derived from the prefixes of the letter] bet, but rather to the body of the verse [itself], for hide, fleece, and jugs are indeed not edible items:
